blocks.raw: # Generating a React Container
blocks.text: Generating a React Container

blocks.raw: This process sets up a container and generates the entire component with index, messages, styles, reducer, saga, actions and constants files, allowing you to develop and add UI elements easily. This eliminates the need to refer to or copy other boilerplate components.
blocks.text: This process sets up a container and generates the entire component with index, messages, styles, reducer, saga, actions and constants files, allowing you to develop and add UI elements easily. This eliminates the need to refer to or copy other boilerplate components.

blocks.raw: To generate a react component, follow these steps:
blocks.text: To generate a react component, follow these steps:

blocks.raw:
1. Navigate to your project directory and open a terminal interface.
2. Run the following command:
   ```
   npm run generate
   ```
3. Choose the generator type from the options.
blocks.text: Navigate to your project directory and open a terminal interface.Run the following command:npm run generateChoose the generator type from the options.

  ### Note:

  The types of generators available are:

  | **Generator** | **Description**                                                                        | **Example**                                                                                    |
  | :------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | **Organisms** | Larger UI components composed of smaller components.                                   | A header with a search bar and navigation links                                                |
  | **Pages**     | Containers that include various elements and other components to form a complete page. | A dashboard page containing charts, tables, and other widgets.                                 |
  | **Templates** | Predefined layouts or structures with placeholders for content.                        | An analytics dashboard template with sections for graphs, user metrics, and recent activities. |
</Callout>

blocks.raw: # Pushing Data to Google Tag Manager
blocks.text: Pushing Data to Google Tag Manager

blocks.raw: To facilitate [FullStory ](https://developer.fullstory.com/overview/api-basics/)integration, you can push data to [Google Tag Manager](https://support.google.com/tagmanager/answer/6102821?hl=en) (GTM).
blocks.text: To facilitate FullStory integration, you can push data to Google Tag Manager (GTM).

blocks.raw:
* During the project setup, specify the Google Analytics (GA) and GTM tracking IDs when prompted by the CLI tool. This will configure the tracking IDs in the code.
* Use the [pushDataToGTM ](https://developers.google.com/tag-platform/tag-manager/datalayer)utility or [window.dataLayer.push ](https://developers.google.com/tag-platform/tag-manager/datalayer#custom_data_layer_methods)(Ex. Cap.js) to push events with data to GTM.

blocks.text: To update the Vulcan SDK follow these steps:

blocks.raw:
1. Open the project folder on your local machine and navigate to the `package.json` file in the root folder.
2. Update the version number under the `@capillarytech/vulcan-react-sdk` package.
3. Open a terminal in your project directory and run the following command:
   ```shell
   npm install
   ```
